name: Kevin J. Scott
title: Chief Technology Officer
talkTitle: Keynote
bio: Kevin J. Scott is the Chief Technology Officer of the PGA of America.

name: Leon Noel
title: Managing Director
talkTitle: Never Click Apply. Get Hired.
bio: Leon Noel is the Managing Director of Engineering at Resilient Coders, a nonprofit that trains Black and Brown engineers and places them into software engineering careers. He is best known for creating #100Devs, a free software engineering bootcamp whose global community has grown to more than 50,000 developers. Earlier in his career he co-founded SocialSci, a scientific surveying platform used by over 4,000 academic institutions, and he has guest lectured at Harvard Business School and MIT Sloan.

name: Danny Thompson
title: Conference Organizer
talkTitle: Keynote
bio: Join Danny Thompson for brief closing remarks to wrap up the conference.

name: Anupama Pathirage
title: Director of Engineering
talkTitle: Building Intelligent Integration Flows: From Natural Language to Execution with Ballerina
bio:
Anupama Pathirage is the Director and Head of Engineering – Integration at WSO2, leading the development of the Ballerina Programming Language and the WSO2 Integration Platform from Austin, Texas. With over 14 years of experience in the software industry, she has played a key role in shaping Ballerina and contributing to various software development projects.

She holds a Master’s degree in Software Architecture and a first-class honors Bachelor’s degree from the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at the University of Moratuwa. In addition to her technical work, she writes for publications such as InfoWorld, DZone, InfoQ, and Medium, and frequently speaks at international conferences.

name: Miguel Guillén
title: Sr Director Technology and Data
talkTitle: Data Governance in the AI age
bio: Miguel Guillen Sr Director Technology and Data

name: Bree Hall
title: Senior Developer Content Lead
talkTitle: Give Your Agent a Second Brain (and a UI to Match)
bio: Bree is a frontend Software Engineer turned Developer Advocate at HubSpot. She has a passion for coding and making technology more accessible to everyone. Bree creates technical content to help developers create and build autonomously. When she isn't working for the Developer Advocacy team at HubSpot, you can find her playing video games, baking, or traveling to magical destinations.

name: Alexander Crettenand
title: Vice President of Software Engineering
talkTitle: Herding Engineers: What I learned from Horse Trainers In Northern Texas
bio: Alexander Crettenand is Vice President of Software Engineering at ADT, where he leads software engineering for the company's smart home security platform. In 2026 he became one of ADT's representatives on the Board of Directors of the Connectivity Standards Alliance — the organization behind Matter, Zigbee, and Aliro — sitting alongside representatives from Apple, Google, Amazon, and Samsung. Before ADT he spent roughly a decade at Google as a Senior Engineering Manager.

name: Patrick Hulce
title: ML Architect
talkTitle: Deploy Your Own VideoGen Model
bio: Patrick has been working at the intersection of AI, visual media, and the web for nearly 20 years. An avid open source contributor with over 30 million downloads and a dozen projects to his name, Patrick now serves as an ML Architect for Studio Media Algorithms at Netflix where he works on the next generation of content creation tools.

name: Zackary Chapple
title: Co-Founder & CEO
talkTitle: If You’re Not Shipping, You’re Not a Leader
bio: Zackary Chapple is the Co-Founder and CEO of Zephyr Cloud, a platform for deploying, orchestrating, and observing micro-frontends at global scale. A veteran of the JavaScript tooling ecosystem, he serves on the Module Federation core team and the Tauri board, and contributes to Rspack. His earlier career spans enterprise architecture at CareerBuilder and a stint as Chief Revenue Officer at Valor Software, giving him a rare dual perspective on engineering at massive scale and scaling a startup from zero to one.

name: Amanda Mayfield
title: Software Engineer
talkTitle: In the age of AI: if it's not Accessible, it's not Acceptable
bio: Amanda Mayfield is a Senior Software Engineer in the DFW area whose passions include Accessibility, Test Driven Development, and Chips & Queso.

name: Yodit Weldegeorgise
title: Java Software Engineer
talkTitle: 5 Mistakes Developers Make When Building Java APIs (and How to Fix Them)
bio:
Yodit Weldegeorgise is a software engineer focused on backend development using Java and modern web technologies. She enjoys building backend services and exploring practical engineering practices that improve system reliability and maintainability.

She actively participates in developer communities, technical meetups, and engineering collaborations where she works with other developers on real-world applications. Through these experiences, she has developed a strong interest in clean API design and backend architecture.

Yodit enjoys sharing practical lessons that help developers write clearer code and design better backend systems.

name: Chris Edgington
title: CEO
talkTitle: Your Browser Has Trust Issues: Why Local Devices Break Modern Web Apps
bio: Chris Edgington is a software engineer based in Central Indiana with 33 years of experience - from device drivers for graphics chips and fast cars, to solving the hard problems of integrating modern software with legacy systems. He's the creator of ProxyBox and spends most of his time these days helping businesses integrate modern software with existing processes across multiple vendors through integration layers and reverse engineering of legacy systems. When not writing code, Chris loves to spend time with family and friends playing ultimate frisbee and KanJam.

name: Prathap Raghavan
title: Director of Product management
talkTitle: From APIs to Agents: Enterprise AI using Java, Ollama & MCP
bio:
Prathap is a seasoned IT professional with over 21 years of experience in system analysis, enterprise software design, development, and testing within complex digital environments. His expertise spans the complete software development lifecycle—from architectural planning to the deployment of scalable, mission-critical applications. He excels at engaging cross-functional stakeholders to define product vision, translating business goals into actionable technology strategies, and aligning initiatives with evolving market demands. His approach is data-driven, consistently leveraging key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess product success, user engagement, and customer satisfaction.
A recognized leader in conversational AI, Prathap has architected and implemented advanced chatbot solutions using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML), enabling highly contextual and human-like user experiences. He has also developed dynamic pricing engines that adjust loan rates in real time, driven by behavioral analytics and real-time risk assessment models. His technical skill set includes strong proficiency in Java, Visual C#, JavaScript, VBScript, and Node.js, alongside extensive experience with integration platforms such as IBM Integration Bus (IIB) and Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA).
In the automation space, Prathap is adept in Robotic Process Automation (RPA) with UiPath, as well as test automation using Selenium (C# and Java) and UFT. His solid command of SQL and NoSQL databases further supports his ability to deliver agile, data-centric solutions across diverse environments.
Beyond technical delivery, Prathap has contributed to the industry through published articles on topics including AI-driven chatbots, AI-based credit risk flows, automation strategy, and transitioning from legacy QA to continuous quality. He has also served as a mentor and judge at hackathons and has peer-reviewed IEEE technical papers. His blend of deep technical expertise, innovation leadership, and industry engagement positions him as a key contributor to enterprise digital transformation.

name: Jerry Reghunadh
title: Senior Director
talkTitle: TBA
bio: I’m an engineer, a passionate problem-solver and lifelong learner.

name: Noah Harris
title: Managing Director
talkTitle: Is Beauty Only Skin Deep?
bio:
Noah is the Managing Director at Radial Agency, an AI consulting firm based in Buffalo, NY. He works at the intersection of engineering execution and executive decision-making, helping organizations adopt AI with the governance, ownership, and delivery rigor required in real businesses. His work spans Fortune 500 and high-growth teams across energy, retail, financial services, automotive, and manufacturing.

Originally from Atlanta, Noah studied Computer Engineering at Georgia Tech. He began his career in 2014 in defense and government-adjacent environments, moved into startups in 2016, and has since supported teams across the country through consulting and hands-on delivery. Today, he advises leaders, builds high-performing teams, and helps engineers turn skill into career momentum through mentorship and meaningful connections.

name: Soujanya Vummannagari
title: Senior Delivery Manager
talkTitle: The Hidden ROI of Caching: Performance Optimization and MIPS Reduction in PBM Engineering
bio:
Soujanya Vummannagari is an accomplished Senior Product/Delivery Manager with over 20 years of experience driving digital transformation across healthcare, retail, finance, and insurance industries. Currently serving as Senior Development Consultant  at Evernorth/Express Scripts through Endava Solutions, she leads a comprehensive product portfolio encompassing 50+ Spring Boot services and 400+ DataPower/Mainframe services while managing a 30+ member global team.
Her expertise spans the full technology spectrum, from legacy mainframe systems (PLI, CICS, COBOL) to modern cloud-native architectures using Java, Spring Boot,Openshift and AWS. Soujanya has demonstrated exceptional leadership in large-scale system modernization, successfully migrating monolithic systems to microservices architectures, achieving 1300+ MIPS savings and delivering $2.5M in license cost reductions through strategic technology transitions.
Notable achievements include developing innovative certification frameworks that contributed to $1.75M in cost savings, building analytics platforms that drove incremental revenue growth, and leading FHIR API migrations that enhanced healthcare data interoperability across multiple organizations. Her technical proficiency extends to DevOps practices, utilizing tools like Jenkins, Git, and Pivotal Cloud Foundry, while maintaining robust monitoring and security standards through Grafana, Splunk, newrelic , and Dynatrace.
Prior to her current role, Soujanya held key positions at Clopay Doors, PNC Healthcare, State Farm Insurance, and Citigroup, where she consistently delivered scalable solutions and led cross-functional teams to achieve strategic business objectives. Her experience includes extensive work with HIPAA compliance, EDI transaction processing, and claims management systems.
Soujanya holds a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering and maintains Project Management Professional (PMP) certification alongside OBIEE Foundation Suite 11G certification, reflecting her commitment to continuous professional development and excellence in technology leadership.

name: Nachiket Desai
title: VP of Applications Engineering and Data
talkTitle: 7 Leadership lessons for the engineer that AI can't replace
bio: Nachiket Desai is VP of Applications Engineering and Data at Smile Doctors, the largest orthodontics-focused dental support organization in the United States, headquartered in Dallas with more than 580 affiliated practices across 36 states. A Dallas-area technology leader, he speaks on applying AI in the enterprise.

name: Belle Duran
title: Data Risk & Compliance Analyst
talkTitle: AI Governance in Financial Services: What Every Developer Should Know
bio: I am a Risk and Compliance Analyst at Texas Capital Bank, where I support operational risk assessments, analytics, and governance frameworks. As a career pivoter with over seven years in financial services, i transitioned from a Business Analyst to a Data Analyst, building expertise in SQL, Python, Tableau, and GRC platforms like RSA Archer. Outside of work, she spoils the most rotten kittens in the world

name: Caleb Jenkins
title: Chief Technology Officer
talkTitle: Software Developer To CTO: AMA! (Ask Me Anything!)
bio: Caleb Jenkins is the Chief Technology Officer at DebtBlue, with prior engineering leadership roles at Microsoft, Charles Schwab, Sabre, and Rocket Mortgage, including leading Developer Experience at Schwab. An international speaker and six-time Microsoft MVP, he has been building with .NET since its beta and is a longtime agile coach and mentor in the developer community. Based in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, he authored the automated unit testing chapter of the Wrox book Real World .NET, C# and Silverlight.

name: Ankita Sood
title: Senior Principal Engineer
talkTitle: Architecting AI in Angular: WebMCP, A2UI, and the Agent Experience
bio: Ankita is a Google Developer Expert in Angular, currently adulting in Austin, Texas . Depending on the weather, she can be found outdoors hiking, biking, paddle boarding, trying to pet other peoples' dogs OR staying indoors reading a book. She has an avid interest in all things Design and Angular. She's been a frontend engineer all her adult working life, which is approximately either 10 years or 100 years, because she has lost sense of time since the pandemic.

name: Chris Sean Dabatos
title: Staff Developer Relations
talkTitle: AI Memory Is Broken And How I Fixed It
bio: Chris is a developer advocate at TiDB with a focus on AI & data infrastructure. He spends a lot of time building AI agents that he actually uses and speaking at meetups and conferences. He’s big on showing, not just telling. So expect real world examples and maybe a few stories about what didn’t work. Outside of work, he runs a YouTube channel, helps organize hackathons, and lives in Las Vegas.

name: Dennis Ivy
title: Developer Advocate
talkTitle: Learn to Code Is at a 5-Year High, and AI Is the Reason
bio: YouTuber, contributor at Traversy Media, developer advocate at Appwrite and online instructor.

name: Nyah Macklin
title: Senior Developer Advocate, Artificial Intelligence
talkTitle: When Vectors Aren’t Enough: Unlocking AI’s Hidden Connections with Graphs
bio: Nyah Macklin is a seasoned researcher and speaker on topics around AI, ML, Ethics, Governance, and Responsibility. Nyah serves as a Senior Developer Advocate for Artificial Intelligence at Neo4j, specializing in context engineering, knowledge graphs, and AI-driven developer tooling where Nyah has built high-impact technical communities and led initiatives that advance a critical understanding of AI and its use cases. They are also the Founder & CTO of Afros in AI, a technical community dedicated to showcasing the multifaceted nature of artificial intelligence. Beyond Nyah's technical expertise, Nyah has a background in government leadership and technology policy, having served as Chief of Staff in the U.S. state government, where they helped shape tech-driven legislative initiatives and equity-driven legislation. When not immersed in their work, Nyah cares about empowering, teaching, and tutoring engineers, live-streaming technical deep dives, and building open-source tools that make software more accessible, explainable, and community-driven.

name: Marino Wijay
title: Solutions Engineer
talkTitle: Fixing Potholes And Broken Roads: Devs Can Troubleshoot the Network With Ops Too!
bio: Marino Wijay is a Canadian, Traveller, International Speaker, and Open Source Advocate and Architect for AI, API Platforms, Service Mesh, Kubernetes, and Networking. He is a CNCF Ambassador,  Organizer for KCD Toronto, and Founder of EmpathyOps. He is passionate about technology and modern distributed systems. He will always fall back to the patterns of Networking and the ways of the OSI. Community building is his driving force; A modern Jedi Academy.

name: Roxy Rodriguez-Becker
title: software engineer, developer advocate
talkTitle: Ship It First, Fix It Later: How a Medical Crisis Led to a Global Tool
bio: Roxy Rodriguez-Becker is a freelance web developer with a background in math education and library science. She created the Tube Feed Tracker PWA for a niche part of the medical community to help thousands of families around the world. Roxy is a Cuban American mother of 3 living in Houston, Texas. She enjoys working out, doing handstands, listening to tech podcasts, and is looking for her next role in tech.

name: Aaron Krauss
title: Techlahoma Organizer & Technical Lead
talkTitle: Building Rapid Web Applications with Laravel + Filament
bio:
Hi, I’m from Oklahoma City, OK, and I’m a technical lead at Clevyr with well over 15 years of experience as a developer. My favorite projects are those that are workflow-heavy involving Laravel, Vue, Tailwind, Flutter, A11y, Ruby, Go, Python, SQL, Swift, Docker, CI/CD, Kubernetes, and more. I'm a big believer in Spec-Driven Development alongside AI tools like Claude Code and Cursor as well.

I organize one of Oklahoma City's largest development-related meetup groups called OKC WebDevs, and have been an active member in the Oklahoma tech community (managed through the non-profit group Techlahoma, with over 8k members) for over a decade now, including as a speaker, organizer, and board member.

Personal project-wise, I'm most actively working on Simple Slides and The Krauss Haus Bar Menu, at least until the next side project comes along.

Other than coding, I like brewing a hot cup of tea, making cocktails, longboarding, eating nutella, and hanging out with my wife and two sons.

name: Avindra Fernando
title: Principal Architect | Fractional CTO
talkTitle: Revolutionize Your Backend: Mastering Server Actions with Next.js and React
bio:
Avindra Fernando is a software consultant with over 13 years of experience helping teams build scalable, modern web applications. In 2021, he founded Taprobane Consulting to guide clients through architectural decisions, migrations to newer tech stacks, and the implementation of robust AI-powered development and testing strategies that ensure quality and performance.

He actively mentors engineering teams, leads workshops, and delivers hands-on training. As a regular speaker at tech conferences, Avindra shares practical lessons on concepts and technologies such as Software Architecture, AI-driven development, React, Next.js, E2E Testing, and TypeScript. He leverages his experience to shape future technology direction and accelerate the growth of companies across industries.

name: Braydon Coyer
title: Senior Frontend Engineer /
talkTitle: Develop Your First Mobile Game Easily with GameSalad

name: Ramiro Beltran
title: Senior Software Engineer
talkTitle: Build Failed Startups—Not Side Projects
bio:
Ram is a Senior/Staff/Lead Frontend Engineer with ten years across the full startup spectrum — from pre-product early-stage to enterprise scale. He builds with a single obsession: the end user. That means reliable systems, clean code, and interfaces that don't make people feel stupid.

He has also spent a decade watching talented engineers and leaders get quietly destroyed by the environments they were planted in — not by a lack of skill, but by a lack of the right conditions. That pattern became the foundation for his upcoming book, Avocado Serial Killer, a leadership memoir about how tech companies lose their best people and what it takes to stop.

He mentors when he can, teaches when he's asked, and is still keeping his avocado trees alive.

name: Sara Baqla
title: Software Engineer
talkTitle: Prickly by Nature: TanStack in the Wild
bio: Sara Baqla holds a Bachelor's and Master's in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology and spent years as an educator before making the leap into software development in 2022. Since then, she has worked across a startup, a creative agency, and now runs her own consultancy, Artemis Bytes LLC, where she builds full stack web and mobile applications for a range of clients.

name: Danyal Mahmud
title: Principal Consultant
talkTitle: From Side Project to Startup: Lessons Learned from Hundreds of Builders
bio:
Danyal Mahmud is a software consultant and the founder of Side Project Society, a community for builders turning side projects into real products and businesses. Over the past four years, he has led the community through monthly meetups, workshops, and community events supporting hundreds of founders, developers, designers, and creators.

With a background in full-stack software development and community building, Danyal brings a practical perspective on what helps early-stage builders move from idea to launch while working full time. His work sits at the intersection of technology, entrepreneurship, and execution.

name: Eunice Kamau
title: Technical Lead
talkTitle: Engineering Real-Time Data Synchronization Across Multi-Cloud Systems
bio:
Eunice Kamau is a distributed systems architect and technical lead with experience designing cloud-based, event-driven, and mission-critical systems across finance, telecommunications, healthcare, and airline environments. Her work focuses on distributed systems architecture, cloud automation, secure data synchronization, reliability, and governance for high-availability platforms.

She is the author of peer-reviewed research on real-time data synchronization in multi-cloud environments, including a published conceptual model addressing latency, consistency, security, interoperability, AI-assisted conflict detection, and secure synchronization across heterogeneous cloud platforms.

name: Srikanth Maru
title: Sr Manager, Data Engineering
talkTitle: From Dashboards to Data Products: A Shift in Thinking
bio:
Srikanth Maru is a distinguished Data Engineering and Architecture Leader with over 17 years of experience transforming data platforms across Fortune 500 enterprises and innovative startups. Currently serving as Senior Manager of Data Engineering & Principal Architect at Cricut Inc., he leads the migration from legacy systems to modern cloud-based platforms that enable advanced AI/ML use cases while managing a team of five data engineers focused on enhancing customer engagement.
His career spans leadership roles at cutting-edge companies including Aeva Inc., where he built data platforms from scratch to support FMCW LiDAR hardware manufacturing, and Samsung Electronics America, where he served as Director of ML Architecture, designing e-commerce data solutions that drove significant revenue growth and developing proprietary forecasting algorithms that reduced stockouts by 20%.
At T-Mobile, Srikanth pioneered custom Hadoop-based ingestion frameworks before commercial data orchestration tools became mainstream, while his tenure at Tata Consultancy Services saw him leading Big Data Centers of Excellence and delivering technical education across global markets including the UK, Australia, and Malaysia.
Srikanth's technical expertise encompasses cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), big data technologies (Hadoop, Spark, Kafka), and modern data tools (Databricks, Snowflake, Airflow). He holds a Bachelor of Engineering from Anna University, India, and is recognized as an early adopter of open-source data frameworks.
His notable achievements include contributing to Walmart's Customer Knowledge Platform serving 200+ million profiles, scaling data platforms for 100+ million customers, and mentoring numerous engineers throughout his career. Srikanth's combination of technical depth, leadership acumen, and international perspective makes him a sought-after architect for enterprise data transformation initiatives.

name: Michael Liendo
title: Staff Developer Advocate
talkTitle: Trust, But Verify: Human-in-the-Loop for Agents That Actually Matter
bio:
As a Staff Developer Advocate at Auth0, I’ve had the opportunity to build applications, develop architectures, and speak around the world as a way to remain customer obsessed. 

Since my beginnings as a self-taught developer, I’ve been focused on simplifying complex scenarios so the barrier to entry becomes a door easily opened for new developers.

name: Anitha Dakamarri
title: Lead Security Engineer
talkTitle: AI-Driven Supply Chain Security: Using AI-BOM to Detect Hidden Vulnerabilities
bio: I am Anitha Dakamarri, a seasoned IT professional with over 19 years of experience in the field of information security. Over the years, I have honed my skills in various domains, including threat modeling, application security assessments, and network security assessments. My work experience spans across reputable organizations like DFIN, USCELLULAR, and Syntel Inc., where I have led teams, developed security standards, and implemented robust security frameworks. hold several industry certifications like CISSP,CISM,CEH,CHFI, which reflect my commitment to continuous learning and professional growth. My passion for security extends beyond technical assessments; I have also initiated and conducted security awareness workshops to educate and empower others. Im active speaker and volunteer at ISACA(CISM Exam development, Mentor ), ISC2(Exam development and UBK panel) OWASP(Contributor),Women4Cyber(Mentor) and WiCys(Mentor).

name: Lawrence Lockhart
title: Senior Developer Advocate
talkTitle: This Isn't The Matrix: Stop Letting Your AI Agents Run Wild
bio: Lawrence Lockhart, Senior Developer Advocate, has been a technologist for 8 years and helping developers reach their goals along the way.  As a mid-life career changer, he appreciates the struggles other adults seeking to transition to tech experience and speaks to those struggles in his content creation on Twitter, TikTok, and Youtube.  He's a saved family man who's truly humbled by where his journey has brought him.

name: Whittington W
title: Staff Software Engineer
talkTitle: Zero to Production: A Simple Technical Framework for Low-Cost Scalable Infrastructure
bio: Army veteran turned software engineer

name: Briana Valmont
title: Senior Engineer
talkTitle: Beyond The Happy Path: Building a BDD Testing Strategy Across Microservices
bio: Briana is an Engineering Team Lead at Citi, where she leads STAR Platform Reliability — driving automated testing strategy across distributed microservices, managing CI/CD pipelines, and mentoring an engineering team. A former Google engineer (Google Pay/Play), she brings deep Java/Spring Boot expertise alongside a full-stack and DevOps toolkit spanning Python, TypeScript, Kubernetes, Kafka, Docker, and BDD frameworks. She is passionate about building systems that scale — both in code and in people — and mentors emerging engineers through CodePath, and TX HerScript. Briana is a community ambassador for Karat BBM as well as TORC, and is the local Austin chapter head for FOSTR.

name: Chris DeMars
title: Senior Developer Advocate
talkTitle: The node_modules Iceberg: Mysteries Below the Waterline
bio: Chris DeMars is a Senior Developer Advocate with over 20 years of technical experience. He speaks all over the world on web accessibility, feature flags, A/B testing, and CSS. For his community contributions, he holds awards as a Progress Champion and former Microsoft MVP, Google Developer Expert, Cloudinary Media Developer Expert, and Auth0 Ambassador. When he is not working on making the web great and accessible you can find him fishing, on the paintball field, rating Detroit Style pizza, and looking for UFO's.

name: Scott McAllister
title: Community Evangelist
talkTitle: Unlocking CI Performance in the Age of Agentic Development
bio: Scott McAllister is a Developer Advocate for Depot. He has been building web applications in several industries for over a decade. Now he's helping others learn about a wide range of web and infrastructure technologies. When he's not coding, writing or speaking he enjoys long walks with his wife, skipping rocks with his kids, and is happy whenever  Seattle Sounders FC, Manchester City, St. Louis Cardinals, Seattle Mariners, Chicago Bulls, Seattle Storm, Seattle Seahawks, Seattle Reign FC, St. Louis Blues, Seattle Kraken, Barcelona, Fiorentina, Borussia Dortmund or Mainz 05 can manage a win.

name: Bethany Ann
title: Software Engineer
talkTitle: The Feature Nobody Used & What It Taught Me About Product Engineering
bio: Bethany is a software engineer who meandered her way into tech after an initial career in art and design. She finally found her happy place when she combined her creative roots with software engineering, discovering a passion for the intersection of creativity and technology. As a product engineer, she enjoys building thoughtful, user-centered products and championing good design along the way. Outside of work, she enjoys spending time mentoring developers through various volunteer programs or frolicking in the great outdoors.

name: Moeez Khan
title: Software Engineer
talkTitle: The Three Ways AI Agents Fail. Here's How to Fix Yours.
bio:
Moeez, a first-generation learner from a small Asian village, has built a dynamic and multidisciplinary journey through technology, education, and leadership. During college, Moeez completed 6 software engineering internships, collaborated with 9 international educational institutions to teach over 2200 underrepresented and privileged students, founded both a tech education and an e-commerce start-up, led 6 college student bodies, pursued 2 global sports semi-professionally, and developed over 85 technical projects before graduating in the class of 2024. 

Currently, Moeez is building AWS Transform, an Agentic AI service focused on transforming .NET, mainframe, and VMware workloads. This work centers on accelerating enterprise modernization across full-stack Windows, mainframe, and VMware systems, alongside enabling custom transformations of APIs, codebases, frameworks, and more.

Aside from technical responsibilities, Moeez actively participates in Amazon hackathons and mentors junior engineers, finding fulfillment in guiding their career paths. Moeez also champions diversity and inclusion, advocating for greater equality within the tech industry. Through these efforts, Moeez positions himself not only as a technical contributor but also as a catalyst for meaningful and lasting change.

name: William Hill
title: Forward Deployed Engineer
talkTitle: The Put That Sh*t On Agent: Building Multi-Agent AI Systems That Actually Talk to Each Other*
bio: Everyone's building AI agents. But most of them can't talk to each other. They're islands. In this session, we'll walk through a real multi-agent system built with Google's Agent Development Kit and the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol: a wardrobe recommendation app that pulls live weather data, reasons a...

name: Corey Weathers
title: Sr Engineer Manager - DevRel
talkTitle: Teach Your To-Do List to Listen
bio: The to-do list is one of the classic first projects for developers. In this hands-on workshop, we will make it talk back to us. Using JavaScript and Deepgram's Voice Agent API, you'll wire speech-to-text, an LLM, and text-to-speech together over a single WebSocket, then add items by voice, interrupt...

name: Ojus Save
title: Developer Relations
talkTitle: Close the Tab: Build Jobs That Keep Running
bio: Ojus Save is a Developer Relations engineer at Render, the cloud platform for deploying full-stack apps and, increasingly, AI workloads. Before Render, he was a Developer Advocate at Zoom, where he championed developers building on the Zoom Developer Platform and worked across REST APIs, authorization, and the app marketplace. An active community member and member of the Postman Leader Program, he is a frequent conference and meetup speaker, and runs his personal site at saveoj.us — his own name, reversed into a domain.

name: Stacy Haven
title: VP of Engineering
talkTitle: Stop Writing the Analysis Script: Let the Data Decide What to Look At
bio: Stacy Haven is VP of Engineering at SAP. Outside of work he runs a market-data platform he originally built for a family member — a system that has been quietly collecting minute-by-minute data for years, which is how he ended up caring a great deal about what to do with more data than anyone can read.

name: Eric Bible
title: Software Engineer III
talkTitle: Why Your Bug Rate Isn’t a Code Problem: Engineering for Unstable Work Intake
bio:
Eric is a Senior Frontend Engineer working on high-traffic e-commerce platforms, focused on delivery systems, release stability, and cross-team integration challenges.

With over 15 years of experience across ops and project management intersecting with frontend development and system design, he specializes since 2020 in building resilient workflows in environments where requirements, dependencies, and priorities are constantly shifting.

His work centers on improving delivery predictability through CI/CD strategy, content decoupling, and intake validation systems — helping teams ship faster by reducing rework and instability.

Outside of his day job, Eric consults on web and low-code solutions for regional businesses and is passionate about applying engineering systems thinking to real-world problems.

name: Quincy Larson
title: Founder
talkTitle: How to Use Scaffolding to Make Your Coding Agents Less Dumb
bio: Quincy Larson is the founder of freeCodeCamp.org, a nonprofit that has helped millions of people around the world learn to code for free through its open-source curriculum, publication, and YouTube channel with over 11 million subscribers. A teacher at heart, he worked as a school director for six years before teaching himself to code, then launched freeCodeCamp in 2014. He also hosts the freeCodeCamp Podcast, where he interviews developers and founders about their journeys into tech.

name: Jacob Orshalick
title: Principal Consultant
talkTitle: Claude Skills: Automate the Boring Stuff
bio: Founder of Focus DEV Solutions with software consulting experience spanning over 2 decades.  Author, speaker, and award winning open source contributor.  Helped launch, grow, turn around, and stabilize software projects during periods of organizational change and market disruption.

name: Michael Gyarmathy
title: Principal Software Engineer
talkTitle: The Evolution of Divot: How Agents Earn Their Autonomy
bio: Michael Gyarmathy is a Principal Software Engineer at PGA of America, based at the association's home in Frisco, Texas, where he joined in 2020 to help stand up a new digital products team. He leads development on PGA Coach, a platform that helps golf teaching professionals run and modernize their businesses, after spending roughly five years in software consulting across a range of industries. Notably, he wasn't a golfer when PGA of America hired him — he deliberately immersed himself in the game to understand his customers firsthand, an approach he credits as central to his customer-obsession engineering philosophy. Outside of work, he enjoys live music, distance running, and breakfast for dinner.

name: Derrick Bozkurt
title: SRE Manager
talkTitle: Stop Prompting, Start Looping: Principles of Loop Engineering
bio: Derrick Bozkurt is a Site Reliability Engineering Manager at RingCentral, where he leads teams keeping large-scale cloud communications infrastructure running reliably. Based in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, he brings a practitioner's perspective on applying agentic AI workflows to real infrastructure and operations work.

name: Nick Taylor
title: Developer Advocate
talkTitle: Build your First MCP App
bio: Nick is a Microsoft MVP, GitHub Star, AWS Community Builder, Software Developer, and Developer Advocate. With over two decades in technology and a decade of open source contributions, plus six years of professional open source work at companies like OpenSauced, dev.to, Netlify and now Pomerium, he brings deep community knowledge to his work. You'll often find him live streaming tech content, either solo or with friends from the community.

name: Mark Mackenzie

name: Venkata Kartheek Reddy Somasani
title: Information Technology Security Engineer
talkTitle: Secure Coding Meets Critical Infrastructure Defense in Water Systems
bio:
Venkata Kartheek Reddy Somasani is an accomplished Information Technology Security and Cybersecurity Engineer with over nine years of specialized experience designing, implementing, and securing enterprise-scale network infrastructures across on-premises and cloud environments. Based in Dallas, Texas, he has built a distinguished career focused on protecting critical public sector systems and safeguarding sensitive government operations.
Since May 2018, Venkata has served the City of Dallas through KC Synergy Solutions Inc., where he plays a pivotal role in securing vital municipal infrastructure. His responsibilities include comprehensive cybersecurity defense for the Dallas Police Department and Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS), ensuring the protection of sensitive law enforcement data through multi-layered security controls such as OKTA two-factor authentication, advanced VPN architectures, and strict CJIS compliance. He has engineered secure, disaster-resilient communication channels between CAD911 dispatch systems and the Texas Department of Public Safety, ensuring uninterrupted emergency response coordination statewide.
One of Venkata’s most significant accomplishments is the architecture of a secure, multi-zoned SCADA network for Dallas’s freshwater, wastewater, and stormwater treatment facilities. By implementing air-gapped environments, zero-internet-access zones, and IDS/IPS protections, he has directly safeguarded critical public health infrastructure from cyber threats. His expertise was further demonstrated during a major ransomware incident, where he successfully detected, contained, and eradicated malware by isolating compromised systems and blocking communication with the Royal ransomware group.
Venkata’s technical expertise spans Cisco ASA, Firepower Threat Defense, SD-WAN, Palo Alto firewalls, F5 BIG-IP, and web application firewalls. He has architected secure hybrid cloud environments using AWS Direct Connect, Azure ExpressRoute, and IPSEC tunnels, supported by AWS architect level certifications. He holds a Master’s degree in Information Assurance and maintains advanced certifications, including CJIS Level 4 and Cisco Firepower NGFW, consistently ensuring compliance with NIST and federal cybersecurity standards.

David Parry is an accomplished Principal Architect with over 25 years of experience in software development, spanning enterprise systems, cloud architecture, and emerging AI integration technologies. His journey began in 1996 when he discovered the fascinating world of programming through Java applets—a technology that, while now obsolete, sparked a lifelong passion for building software that connects people to information and services.
Throughout his illustrious career, David has been involved in numerous high-profile projects that demonstrate his ability to deliver scalable, reliable systems under demanding conditions. He has successfully built and implemented content management systems for a wide range of global clients, including the prestigious Johnnie Walker brand and its renowned keepwalking.com platform. These projects required not only deep technical expertise but also an understanding of how technology serves brand storytelling and customer engagement at scale.
As a consultant at a Big 4 firm, David played a pivotal role in solving critical issues for enterprise customers across industries. He developed a reputation for diagnosing complex problems in high-traffic web platforms and architecting solutions that balanced immediate business needs with long-term technical sustainability. This consulting experience sharpened his ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and to navigate the organizational dynamics that often determine whether technology initiatives succeed or fail.
Never one to shy away from innovation, David has continuously expanded his skills to embrace emerging technologies. He has worked extensively on mobile applications and embedded Android TV systems, delivering streaming services that provide customers with exceptional viewing experiences. These projects demanded expertise in performance optimization, real-time data handling, and the unique constraints of embedded environments—skills that translate directly to modern distributed systems and edge computing architectures.
Currently, David holds the position of Principal Architect at Qodo.ai, where he oversees strategic planning and execution of architectural designs for customers building AI-powered development tools. His current focus includes integrating large language model APIs with enterprise Java systems using Spring AI, designing Model Context Protocol server architectures, and building the infrastructure that enables AI agents to interact securely with external tools and data sources. This work sits at the intersection of his deep Java expertise and the rapidly evolving landscape of AI-assisted software development.
David is passionate about sharing knowledge with the developer community. He actively contributes to open-source projects and speaks at conferences about practical approaches to AI integration, cloud architecture, and Java development patterns. His workshop on building MCP servers from scratch reflects his teaching philosophy: developers learn best by building real systems, understanding protocols at the wire level, and debugging their way to mastery.
Having witnessed the evolution of Java development from applets to microservices to AI-native architectures, David brings a rare combination of historical perspective and forward-looking vision to every project. His wealth of experience, strategic mindset, and hands-on technical skills make him an invaluable asset to any organization navigating the complexities of modern software architecture. When he's not architecting systems, David enjoys mentoring junior developers and exploring how AI can augment—rather than replace—human creativity in software development.
